Name: Watering Path V2
Author: slpOff
Description:
[font=Comic Sans MS]# WateringPathV2[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]This mod is less about manually watering every tile every day, and more about designing water routes and managing moisture across your farm.[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]Crops do not just care whether the soil is wet or dry. Their growth can change depending on how much moisture they are actually getting.[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]In practice, that means the important skill here is not swinging the watering can more often, but learning how moisture spreads, where it weakens, and how to build fields around that.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]## How To Approach It[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]The basic idea is simple:[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]- Water tiles, sprinklers, and paddy soil act as moisture centers.[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Soil closer to those centers tends to hold stronger moisture.[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Soil farther away becomes weaker.[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Moisture does not instantly disappear the next day, so the goal is not just "water it once," but "maintain a stable moisture pattern over time."[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]Because of that, it helps to stop thinking of a field as one uniform block.[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]It is usually better to think in terms of wetter zones, weaker zones, and transition zones.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]## Recommended Playstyle[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]### 1. Decide on your water centers first[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]Before expanding a field, decide what the moisture anchor will be.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]- A river, pond, or canal edge[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- A sprinkler position[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- A paddy line that will carry moisture through the field[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]If that anchor is vague, the field may look large and efficient, but the actual moisture flow will break apart in the middle.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]### 2. Do not spread too wide too early[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]The farther a field stretches, the more likely moisture will weaken.[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]Instead of starting with a huge rectangle, it is usually better to stabilize a smaller plot close to the source first.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]- Put moisture-sensitive crops near the center[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Use more forgiving crops toward the outside[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Leave uncertain edge tiles for testing[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]That makes it much easier to read how your field is behaving.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]### 3. Treat paddy soil as a moisture line, not decoration[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]Paddy soil is not just a visual theme. It works best when you use it as part of the farm's moisture structure.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]- Start it near real water or a sprinkler-supported section[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Use it on tiles that act as the waist or spine of the field[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Avoid isolated paddy tiles with no real source behind them[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]If a paddy tile no longer meets its conditions, it can fall back to normal soil the next day.[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]So it is safest to build paddy soil as a connected route, not as scattered accents.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]### 4. Do not plant everything anywhere[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]Different crops may end up preferring different moisture ranges.[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]Even inside the same field, one area may stay too wet while another stays borderline dry.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]A practical way to handle that is:[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]- Strong, stable moisture areas: candidates for more demanding crops[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Mid-range moisture areas: general-use crops[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Weak outer edges: testing, low-risk crops, or empty buffer space[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]If a crop behaves strangely, it is often better to question the tile before questioning the seed.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]### 5. Think of fertilizer as setting up nodes, not painting the whole field[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]Spread fertilizer can travel through paddy networks, but it weakens with distance.[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]Because of that, it usually feels better to build small influence points in important zones instead of expecting one center tile to cover everything.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]- A zone focused on faster growth[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- A zone focused on better quality[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- A zone where moisture retention matters most[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]This gives different parts of the field distinct roles instead of making everything feel the same.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]## Good Things To Check Each Morning[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]At the start of the day, it helps to quickly inspect:[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]- Whether the line from water or sprinklers is still intact[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Whether a missing middle tile broke the moisture chain[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Whether any paddy soil downgraded back into normal soil[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Whether crops on the weak edges are starting to react badly[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]This mod rewards checking structure, not just checking whether the dirt looks wet.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]## Who This Mod Fits Best[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]- Players who want less watering-can labor, but do not want farming to become fully automatic[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Players who enjoy designing rice fields, canals, lanes, and shaped farm layouts[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Players who like managing crop placement rather than treating every tile the same[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]- Players who want field position to matter[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]## Installation[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]1. Install SMAPI.[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]2. Put this mod into your `Mods` folder.[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]3. If needed, adjust moisture thresholds and paddy-related settings through GMCM.[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]## In One Line[/font]

[font=Comic Sans MS]This is not just a mod about watering. It is a mod about running a moisture system.[/font]
[font=Comic Sans MS]If you build around water centers, place crops intentionally, and use paddy soil and fertilizer as connected support structures, the farm becomes much more interesting to manage.[/font]
